stem: A 23-year-old woman has worn latex gloves daily for 2 years as a nursing assistant. Two days after a long shift, she has itchy, red, swollen skin on both hands and wrists that stops sharply at the glove line. She has no wheeze, fever or joint pain.
oneliner: 23F + latex gloves for 2 years + itchy red swollen hands to the glove line 2 days after a shift → ?
ask: Which hypersensitivity mechanism is most likely?

options.B: Type II (antibody to cell or matrix antigen)

whyNot.A: Type I appears **within minutes** of contact; her rash appeared 2 days after the shift
whyNot.B: Type II needs **antibody against a cell or matrix antigen** (hemolysis, cytopenia, one target organ); she has a rash only where the gloves touched
whyNot.C: Type III is **systemic, with fever, joint pain and low complement**; she has none of these
whyNot.E: Direct mast cell activation is **immediate and needs no sensitization**; her rash appeared 2 days after exposure

why: A rash confined to the area of contact that appears 48 to 72 hours later means **sensitized T cells** have been recalled to the skin. Latex can cause both type IV and type I reactions; the timing tells them apart.

head: Effector
Timing
Typical lesion or test
Classic examples
rows: Type I (IgE, mast cell)
IgE on mast cells; histamine and tryptase release
**Minutes**
Wheals and wheeze; skin prick test, raised tryptase
Anaphylaxis, hay fever, asthma, food allergy
Type II (antibody to cell or matrix antigen)
**IgG or IgM against a cell-surface or matrix antigen**, complement
Minutes to hours
**Linear immunofluorescence**; positive direct Coombs test
Rh and ABO hemolysis, Goodpasture, Graves, myasthenia gravis
Type III (immune complex)
Antigen-antibody complexes, complement, neutrophils
1 to 2 weeks after first exposure; hours on re-exposure (Arthus)
**Granular, lumpy deposits; low C3 and C4**
Serum sickness, SLE, post-streptococcal GN, polyarteritis nodosa
Type IV (T cell, delayed)
**Sensitized T cells** (no antibody)
48 to 72 hours
Vesicles or induration; patch test, tuberculin
Poison ivy, nickel, tuberculin test, GVHD

idea.rule: Rash at the contact site 2 to 3 days later = type IV, T cell mediated.
also: Nickel, latex, poison ivy and the tuberculin test are all type IV
